restated_task: Add an instance method `Version.is_compatible(other) -> bool` to the Version class in src/semver/version.py. The method returns True when `new` (the argument) can be used in place of `old` (self). Compatibility rules: majors must be equal; new.minor >= old.minor; prerelease parts must be equal (both None counts as equal); patch is ignored. Major 0 versions are special: only compatible with an identical version (major, minor, patch, prerelease all equal). If `other` is not a Version instance (subclasses allowed), raise TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got' followed by the type. Include a docstring with at least two doctest examples. Do not modify any other public behavior, tests, docs, or packaging files; the existing pytest suite must continue to pass.

interface_contract.name: Version.is_compatible
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if `other` is compatible with `self` per semantic versioning compatibility rules. Compatibility is defined as: (1) self.major == other.major; (2) other.minor >= self.minor; (3) self.prerelease == other.prerelease (both None counts as equal); (4) patch is ignored. Special case: if self.major == 0, then compatibility requires exact equality of major, minor, patch, and prerelease (build is still ignored). The method accepts Version subclasses as valid `other` arguments.
error_cases: TypeError: raised when `other` is not an instance of Version (or a subclass). Message format: 'Expected a Version type but got <class '...'>' (e.g., "Expected a Version type but got <class 'str'>").

acceptance_criteria: Version(1, 2, 4).is_compatible(Version(1, 2, 3)) is True (patch ignored, symmetric for patch)
Version(0, 1, 0).is_compatible(Version(0, 1, 1)) is False (major 0 requires exact match including patch)
Version(1, 0, 0).is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0, 'rc1')) is False (prerelease absent vs present)
Version(1, 0, 0, 'rc1').is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0)) is False (prerelease present vs absent)
Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible('wrongtype') raises TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got'
Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible({'a': 2}) raises TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got'
Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible([]) raises TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got'
